### Career Regular-Season Points Per Game Comparison

* **Michael Jordan:** **30.1** points per game [T1].
* **LeBron James:** **26.8** points per game [T1].

---

### Key Factual Context and Tradeoffs

1. **Per-Game Scoring Rate vs. Total Games and Longevity**
   * **Michael Jordan** holds the higher regular-season scoring average at 30.1 PPG across 1,072 games and 15 seasons [T1], [T2], complemented by 10 NBA scoring titles [jordan_scoring_0].
   * **LeBron James** averages 26.8 PPG across 1,622 games and 23 seasons [T1], [T3]. While his per-game average is 3.3 points lower than Jordan's, James maintained a scoring average of at least 25 points per game in all 19 seasons following his rookie year [lebron_scoring_160], [lebron_scoring_240] and became the NBA's all-time leading scorer [lebron_scoring_240].

2. **High-Scoring Game Frequencies**
   * **30+ Point Games:** LeBron has 577 games [T3]; Jordan has 562 games [T2].
   * **40+ Point Games:** Jordan leads with 173 games [T2]; LeBron has 79 games [T3].
   * **50+ Point Games:** Jordan leads with 31 games [T2]; LeBron has 14 games [T3].

---

### Distinction Between Factual Evidence and Subjective Judgments

* **Factual Evidence:** Jordan holds a higher career regular-season scoring average (30.1 vs. 26.8) and achieved more 40- and 50-point regular-season games [T1], [T2], [T3]. LeBron has sustained elite scoring over a substantially larger regular-season sample (1,622 games vs. 1,072 games) [T2], [T3], leading to the all-time total points record [lebron_scoring_240].
* **Subjective Assessment:** Determining whether Jordan’s higher per-game scoring average and peak scoring performances outweigh LeBron’s sustained longevity and total volume in "Greatest of All Time" (GOAT) evaluations is a subjective debate dependent on individual criteria rather than an objective statistical fact.
